newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel set for confrontation with Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel set for confrontation with Palestinians.

text.p: Israel was poised on Wednesday to approve construction of a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem despite international protests and warnings of Palestinian violence.
"The struggle for Jerusalem has begun," Police Minister Avigdor Kahalani said. "When we decide today, we will make it clear once and for all that Jerusalem is the capital of the Jewish people."

A ministerial committee was scheduled to convene at 1230 GMT to approve a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel, a tree-covered hill captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

In a bid to blunt Arab anger, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke by telephone with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak before the meeting about the project condemned by Palestinians as a violation of peace deals with Israel.
Palestinians see it as an attempt to pre-empt the final status of Jerusalem, which is supposed to be decided in future talks that must be completed by 1999.

"Prime Minister Netanyahu...(told Mubarak that Israel) intends to build about 2,000 housing units for Jews in the Har Homa neighbourhood on land which is largely private and under Jewish ownership," a spokesman said, referring to the project's first stage.
"(The government) also intends to build in the next three years 3,000 housing units for Arabs in Jerusalem," he said, repeating a pledge by Netanyahu.

Palestinians and Israeli leftists have warned the plan could ignite Arab rage like September clashes after Netanyahu opened a tunnel entrance near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israelis died in that violence, which almost destroyed the Israel-PLO peace process.
"There are scenarios that say there will be riots and possibly the opening of fire -- we are not naive," Kahalani told Army Radio.
Major-General Uzi Dayan, commander of Israeli forces in the West Bank, said the army had not sent reinforcements to the area but had "concentrated troops in the necessary places".
Israeli security sources said an army plan in the event of clashes called for deploying tanks and snipers in areas of the West Bank and Gaza still under military occupation.

The U.N. Security Council expressed concern on Tuesday over Israel's settlement policy in East Jerusalem and said it hoped "restraint and wisdom would prevail so as not to undo the peace process", council president Njuguna Mahugu of Kenya said.

But Netanyahu's chief of communications, David Bar-Illan, said: "It is a civil project which intends to alleviate the housing shortage (in Jerusalem). It is good for the Jews. It is good for the Arabs."
Palestinians, who want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state, said the plan would wreck the foundations of their peace deal with Israel.

"Things are already hot in the West Bank and could blow up at any moment. All that's needed is a spark and Jabal Abu Ghneim could be that spark," Faisal al-Husseini, the top Palestinian Authority official in Jerusalem, said on Israel Television.

On Tuesday, Israeli undercover soldiers killed a 60-year-old Palestinian and wounded three others in a village north of Jerusalem after being cornered by stone-throwers, the army said. Palestinians said the soldiers, dressed in civilian clothes, had provoked residents.
Israel handed parts of the Gaza Strip and West Bank to Palestinian rule under peace deals signed since 1993 but Israeli soldiers still patrol other areas.
